item.title: Inspectors demand urgent action on youth detention centres
item.description:
Inspectors demand urgent action on youth detention centres

September 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Staff shortages at the Dutch youth detention centres are putting detainees and staff under “persistent and serious” pressure and threatening their safety, three government inspectorates have warned.

Around 450 young people who have been convicted of a crime or are suspected of one are held in the country’s six youth detention centres, known as JJIs. The centres take young people who were aged between 12 and 23 when they committed the offence, though most are between 14 and 21.

Unlike adult prisons, they are meant to focus on education and treatment rather than punishment, to reduce the risk of reoffending.

In a letter to junior justice minister Claudia van Bruggen, the justice, education and health and youth care inspectorates said young people held in the centres are the victims of an “ever-increasing, worrying” erosion of care, treatment, education and daily activities. They called for an urgent action plan.

“Temporary emergency measures such as a shortened daily programme have now become standard practice,” said Elske van Amelsfort, chief inspector at the justice and security inspectorate. “That is why an action plan is needed from the state secretary in the short term.”

By law, young people in JJIs should spend 77 hours a week in group activities. Emergency measures introduced in 2023 set a reduced floor of 62 hours. The inspectorates said the centres are not meeting the requirements of either, because daily programmes are regularly cut back or cancelled at short notice when staff are unavailable.

As a result, young people spend too much time in their rooms, miss school and leave, and cannot always contact their families. Young people told inspectors they found it frustrating to be kept in their rooms, often without warning, and that repeatedly broken promises made it harder to stay motivated.

Warning signs
The inspectorates also said staff are becoming less experienced and more overstretched. Staff are regularly moved at short notice to units where they do not know the young people, which makes it harder to spot warning signs in time. The constant turnover of supervisors is causing frustration and tension among both young people and staff.

The inspectorates have raised concerns about the centres since 2019. The decision to phase out freelance staff in 2025 made the staffing crisis worse, the letter said.

In July, children’s ombudsman Margrite Kalverboer said there had been barely any improvement since the inspectorates’ previous warning a year earlier. She said almost all children’s rights were being violated in the youth detention centres.

item.title: Pro tables bill to remove abortion from Dutch criminal code
item.description:
Pro tables bill to remove abortion from Dutch criminal code

September 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Opposition party Pro has put forward a bill to remove abortion from the Dutch criminal code and officially regulate it as a part of healthcare. Currently, abortion is still technically a crime, although allowed under specific circumstances by professionals.

MP Lisa Vliegenthart, a former midwife, handed the bill to campaigners from feminist group Dolle Mina outside parliament on Monday morning, broadcaster NOS reported.

“This is incredibly important because abortion is healthcare, and as far as I am concerned healthcare has no place in the criminal code,” she said. “That is why we want to remove abortion from the criminal code and include it in healthcare legislation.”

Already legal
Abortion has been legal in the Netherlands since the 1980s, but the legal framework is unusual. Under an article of the criminal code, performing an abortion is a crime. The exception is if it is carried out by a doctor in a licensed clinic or hospital under the conditions set out in the Termination of Pregnancy Act.

Those conditions include a limit of 24 weeks and a requirement that the woman indicates she is in a situation of distress. Women themselves cannot be prosecuted for having abortions, but people administering them can be.

Pro says it wants to keep all the current care requirements, including the time limit, but move them into healthcare law. “Of course abortion has to be carried out carefully,” Vliegenthart said. “But you don’t need the criminal code for that.”
Proponents of the bill say that having abortion in the criminal code adds to the stigma around it and makes the rules harder to update.

The current law was a hard-fought compromise, passed by 76 votes to 74 in the lower house in 1980 and by 38 to 37 in the Senate. The rules have since been loosened, with the mandatory five-day waiting period was scrapped in 2023, and family doctors can now prescribe the abortion pill.

VVD support
Whether the bill passes depends largely on the right-wing liberal VVD. In 2023, the VVD joined the CDA, ChristenUnie, PVV, SGP and FvD to vote down a similar attempt to remove abortion from the criminal code. But its 2025 election manifesto committed the party to “actively work” to do so.

With support from the VVD, D66 and smaller opposition parties, the bill could have a narrow majority. However, the parties’ coalition partner, the CDA, remains against it.

The VVD has not yet said whether it will back the bill. “We are going to read the proposal and wait for the Council of State’s response,” the party said.

Constitution
If the bill passes, Pro wants to go further and enshrine the right to abortion in the Dutch constitution, as France did in 2024. Vliegenthart pointed to the United States, where the Supreme Court overturned the federal right to abortion in 2022. “That pressure exists in Europe and the Netherlands too,” she said.

In practice, access rather than legality is often the bigger issue for women. Last month, the health inspectorate allowed the country’s only online abortion service, which now issues around a quarter of all abortion pills, to keep operating after it changed its practices.

item.title: Market watchdog calls for transparency on AI in price setting
item.description:
Market watchdog calls for transparency on AI in price setting

September 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch consumer markets authority ACM has called for more transparency on the role of AI in setting ticket prices after an investigation found wide discrepancies in the amounts charged for airline tickets.

The ACM said some airline seats had 35 different prices, while one-third of tickets cost 40% more than the average price, but there was no easy way for passengers to find the cheapest fare.

ACM chairman Martijn Snoep said the investigation into airline tickets was relevant because “similar techniques are being applied in other sectors”. Online retailers, concert ticket sites and even petrol stations are also using AI to set prices.

Commercial companies are using AI to drive dynamic pricing, based on supply and demand and competitors’ rates, but customers are unable to see how the prices are set.

Sometimes two people looking at the same product at the same time can be charged different prices, the ACM said. The impact of AI also means consumers spend longer searching for the best deal.

“We expect that AI and the availability of data means companies will increasingly use computer-aided prices, including personalised prices,” Snoep said.

The ACM has called on companies to be more open about how they set their prices and explain what factors influence the algorithms.

“Transparency is necessary so we can have a public debate about the desirability and the consequences of this development and how we want to proceed, keeping an eye on the way markets function and preventing people’s vulnerabilities being abused.”

item.title: Budget deal in sight after coalition agree to scrap welfare cuts
item.description:
Budget deal in sight after coalition agree to scrap welfare cuts

September 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Coalition parties D66, CDA and VVD hope to have a deal with the opposition parties finalised by Tuesday evening after talks over the weekend brought progress on the key issues of welfare and wealth taxes.

The left-wing parties Pro and Volt said the cabinet had agreed to drop its planned €6 billion cuts to social security in full, a key demand of the two parties and trade unions.

The two-year maximum term for the WW unemployment payments will be retained, while the long-term incapacity benefit WIA will remain untouched.

The government had already abandoned plans to cap benefits such as sick pay and maternity pay at a lower level and raise the retirement age in step with life expectancy.

Volt leader Laurens Dassen said the talks would need to continue to identify where the cabinet plans to find the money that will not be raised from welfare cuts, adding that “the devil is in the detail”.

Capital gains tax

The main concession to parties on the right is the introduction of a capital gains tax to replace the “box 3” asset taxes, which need to be reformed after the Supreme Court ruled that they breached European human rights laws.

The new system is expected to leave a €10 billion hole in the public finances in the short term because assets will only be taxed when they are sold, rather than on their annual gains, as is currently the case.

The Telegraaf, which has seen leaked copies of the plans, said the cabinet planned to raise the “box 2” tax on income from shares and dividends from business owners, to offset the loss.

The right-wing parties JA21 and SGP, who have also teamed up for the negotiations, were less enthusiastic about the proposed deal after meeting prime minister Rob Jetten and finance minister Eelco Heinen on Sunday.

“Nothing about migration”

JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans said the plans were “more left than right”, adding he had heard “nothing about tax cuts, migration or security”.

Chris Stoffer, of the orthodox protestant SGP, said his party’s concerns about abortion and surrogate parenting had also not been addressed.

Jetten and Heinen also held talks with ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker, whose party could act as a go-between for the two sides. Bikker said she had seen “urgency, unity and movement” in the government parties after meeting the ministers on Saturday.

The cabinet needs 10 opposition votes to pass the budget in the lower house and 16 seats in the Senate.

Pro and Volt have 21 seats between them in the Tweede Kamer and just enough senators to secure a majority, while the right-wing duo can only provide enough votes in the lower house.

item.title: Hospitals block access to patients’ records after cyber threat
item.description:
Hospitals block access to patients’ records after cyber threat

September 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Some Dutch hospitals denied patients access to their medical records over the weekend because of security issues with the online gateway Citrix.

The national cybersecurity centre NCSC advised hospitals to disconnect their Citrix applications from the internet after discovering a “critical vulnerability” that could allow hackers to operate the system remotely.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued an alert on Sunday, saying it had “received reports and partner threat intelligence confirming that threat actors are actively exploiting these vulnerabilities globally”.

The Amphia Ziekenhuis in Breda, the Elisabeth-TweeSteden Ziekenhuis in Tilburg and the Frisius medical centre in Leeuwarden were among the Dutch hospitals that reported problems at the weekend.

Doctors were still able to look at patients’ records, but the patients themselves could not during online consultations.

The Frisius MC said on Sunday it had blocked access as a precautionary measure in response to the alerts by the NCSC and Z-Cert, the agency specialising in digital security in healthcare, but its systems were now back online.

The interior ministry said some of its civil servants had been unable to work remotely at the weekend after its Citrix applications were switched off.

It is not the first time Dutch institutions have experienced security issues with Citrix and its access program, NetScaler. Last year the public prosecution service (OM) restricted access for two months after hackers exploited a gap in its security systems.

item.title: Amsterdam top destination for young people leaving home
item.description:
Amsterdam top destination for young people leaving home

September 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Most young people leaving home in the Netherlands head to Amsterdam, according to new figures from national statistics office CBS.

More than 174,000 people aged 18 to 30 moved out of their parents’ home in 2024, and a third of them settled in Amsterdam, one of ten councils tracked by the research. The city drew 12,760, well ahead of Rotterdam and Groningen.

The city was also the most popular destination for students, attracting 5,475, followed by Utrecht and Groningen. Nijmegen had the highest share of students
among young newcomers at 53.1%, followed by Utrecht and Leiden at 49.5% each.

The Hague was the exception: 65.4% of the young people who moved there were not students.

Just under a third of those leaving home were students, and half of them (49.9%) moved into privately rented housing. The rest went into social housing or owner-occupied homes. Non-students were most likely to move into an owner-occupied home (42.6%).

The figures only cover young people registered as living with their parents in the Netherlands at the start of 2024. They exclude anyone who moved to the country from abroad that year, such as newly arrived international students.

item.title: Israel strips Dutch diplomats’ status over settlement goods ban
item.description:
Israel strips Dutch diplomats’ status over settlement goods ban

September 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Israel is revoking the diplomatic status of Dutch diplomats in the West Bank city of Ramallah in the latest pushback against the Netherlands’ ban on goods produced in illegal Israeli settlements in occupied territories.

In a statement on social media, Israeli foreign minister Gideon Saar said the diplomats must return their Israeli-issued diplomatic documents within seven days, after which their diplomatic privileges and immunities will expire. He said the move was intended as a response to the ban that came into force last week.

“If the Netherlands wishes to continue representing its interests with the Palestinians, it may do so from Palestinian Authority territory, rather than from the territory of the State of Israel,” he said.

Dutch foreign minister Berendsen said in response that the move was “unnecessary” and that he “deeply regrets” it, adding that the ban on settlement goods “is not directed at Israel” but rather an obligation to comply with international law.

Last month, Israel expelled two Dutch officials from the US-backed centre in Kiryat Gat that coordinates the Gaza ceasefire.

Settlement ban
The Netherlands is the main EU import hub for goods produced in settlements in the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights – all of which are considered occupied under international law.

The cabinet agreed to the ban in May. It covers imports of and trade in settlement goods, and also applies to Dutch companies operating abroad.

Saar said that “Israel will not ignore measures intended to harm it. Any country that acts in a hostile and unilateral manner against Israel will lose influence and relevance in the region.”

He also spoke of “growing antisemitism and incitement openly seen on the streets of the Netherlands. Not only are this antisemitism and incitement not being seriously addressed, but the anti-Israel policies of the Dutch Government are fueling them.”

Saar did not specify what he was referring to. This spring there were four attacks on Jewish and pro-Israel targets in the Netherlands, which Dutch investigators believe were coordinated by an Iraqi man arrested in the US. Experts have said the attacks were very likely directed by Iran.

Economic ties
Despite the dispute over settlement goods, the Netherlands is the biggest destination for Israeli capital in the world, holding €44.9 billion in investment in 2024 – nearly four times as much as the US, according to research by Amsterdam-based corporate watchdog SOMO.

It is also the world’s second biggest investor into Israel, with €27.3 billion invested there in 2024 alone.

Earlier this month, more than 230 former Dutch ministers, ambassadors, diplomats and civil servants called on the cabinet to take tougher measures against Israel, including a full arms embargo and the suspension of the European Union’s trade agreement with the country.

item.title: Dutch river cruise stranded as Rhine falls to new record levels
item.description:
Dutch river cruise stranded as Rhine falls to new record levels

September 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The river Rhine dropped to a new record low level at the weekend at the Dutch-German border, with no sign of fresh rainfall in the days ahead.

The river measured 6.1m at Lobith, the point where it flows into the Netherlands, on Sunday, below the previous record of 6.12m set in August.

Further upstream in Cologne, a Dutch cruise ship became stuck in mid-river as water levels dropped to just 40 centimetres on the gauge, leaving around 1.5 metres of navigable depth.

The Dutch Melody, which carries 140 passengers, was able to continue downriver after being assisted by another ship, German river police said. The four-deck vessel is due to arrive in Nijmegen later on Monday.

River levels are expected to drop further this week due to low rainfall in the Alps. At Lobith the flow of water has fallen below 600 cubic metres per second for the first time on record.

Dutch water authorities have had to impose restrictions on river traffic as channels became narrower and shallower during the summer drought.

Vessels using the IJssel to travel from Arnhem to Zutphen are having to take a 300km detour after Rijkswaterstaat imposed a one-way system.

Some ferries across the rivers have been cancelled and river cruises have had to cancel trips or shorten their itineraries because sections of the Rhine have become impassable.

item.title: Jetten’s D66 conference speech interrupted by Gaza hecklers
item.description:
Jetten’s D66 conference speech interrupted by Gaza hecklers

September 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Prime minister Rob Jetten’s speech to his D66 party’s weekend conference was interrupted by hecklers protesting against Israel’s military intervention in Gaza.

Jetten was briefly led from the stage by security guards after demonstrators twice shouted out at the start of the speech in the Amsterdam RAI arena on Sunday.

The prime minister initially said the protesters could stay in the conference hall if they sat down “so you don’t bother those sitting behind you”, but after the second interruption a handful of demonstrators were escorted out of the hall.

The demonstrators wore T-shirts with slogans such as Bloedcoalitie (“blood coalition”) and Liberaal/Neutraal/Genocidaal (“liberal, neutral, genocidal”).

Jetten said: “I see that you want to highlight the situation in Gaza and I understand that very much.”

Afterwards he told RTL Nieuws that the protest had been respectful. “The right to demonstrate and have your say is one of the strengths of our democracy, as long as it’s done respectfully, and that’s what we saw here in the hall.”

Budget delays

The conference marked the 60th anniversary of the foundation of D66 and the first time a prime minister had addressed the autumn gathering.

Jetten said his cabinet had made progress in several areas, such as drawing up plans to cut nitrogen pollution and preventing the online government services portal DigiD being sold to an American company.

But he admitted it had taken longer than hoped for his government to make a deal with opposition parties to pass next year’s budget. The minority coalition of D66, CDA and VVD needs the support of at least two other parties in both houses of parliament.

Jetten said he had seen signs during talks last week that parties “from left to right” were prepared to negotiate, proving that “broad co-operation is possible with this generation of politicians”.

The prime minister also insisted he would not give in to the “anti-Dutch forces that want to destroy our democracy from within”, referring to the violent demonstrations in The Hague a week ago that featured “appalling extreme right-wing slogans and even Nazi salutes”.

Jetten vowed that the “wave of optimism” would ultimately triumph over the loudest voices, echoing his predecessor Mark Rutte, who called on people to vote for “doers, not yellers”.

“They might shout louder, but we get more done,” Jetten said.

item.title: Meerdink double gives Xavi first win as Oranje coach in Belgrade
item.description:
Meerdink double gives Xavi first win as Oranje coach in Belgrade

September 27, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Mexx Meerdink’s first two international goals were enough for the Netherlands to edge past Serbia and earn Xavi Hernandez his first win as coach in a gritty encounter in Belgrade.

Meerdink scored from the penalty spot in the first half after Crysencio Summerville was brought down in the area, and slotted the winner midway through the second half in a period when Oranje were dominating.

But there was a blow for Xavi ahead when Cody Gakpo had to be replaced by Ruben van Bommel in the 17th minute after going down under a heavy challenge from Saša Lukici in the penalty area.

The coach said he satisfied with his first week of competitive fixtures, including the 1-1 draw with Germany in Amsterdam on Thursday, but saw plenty of room for improvement.

“I feel happy that we got three points, but we need to play better, especially in the first half,” Xavi said. “Second half we dominated more and attacked the spaces more.

“It’s important to get the three points, but the most important thing is we are generating lots of chances to score and the players feel comfortable with the structure that we have.”

Stodgy first half

Oranje had the better of a stodgy first 45 minutes of their second Nations League fixture, but only occasionally showed a cutting edge. Meerdink was unable to connect properly with Gakpo’s cross in the 15th minute, while a long spell of possession ended with Ryan Gravenberch dragging a shot wide.

The Dutch looked comfortable defending their lead and almost went further ahead when Serbia goalkeeper Vanja Milinkovic-Savic needed all of his 2.02m height to tip Joey Veerman’s inswinging corner over the crossbar.

The home side equalised right at the start of the second half as they poured into the Dutch penalty area, drawing two good saves from Bart Verbruggen. The Oranje defenders were unable to clear their lines and the ball fell to half-time substitute Luka Jovic, who gave Verbruggen no chance from close range.

Dumfries dangerous

The Dutch took a grip on the game with Denzel Dumfries repeatedly finding space down the right, first picking out Van Bommel, whose shot hit the outside of the post, before an even better cross was turned over the crossbar by Tijjani Reijnders.

Meerdink’s winner in the 69th minute was provided by Guus Til, who had just come on as a substitute, as the AZ striker held off the close attentions of his marker to steer the ball into in the far corner.

Jovic remained Serbia’s greatest threat as the hosts pushed for an equaliser, twice flashing headers narrowly wide, while Van Bommel should have put the game beyond reach with a late breakaway, but his tame shot failed to test Milinkovic-Savic.

The Netherlands next play Greece, who beat Serbia 2-1 in their opening match, in Thessaloniki on Thursday.
